pages.text: How does an anomaly begin in physics? With a choice. A field whose potential has two equal valleys must fall into one as the universe cools - and regions too far apart to agree fall into different ones. Where they meet, the field is stuck on the hill between: a $(thing)domain wall$(). With more dimensions of choice you get strings, monopoles and textures - $(thing)topological defects$(), which no smooth change can remove.

The wall's energy is E = ∫[½φ'² + λ(φ² − v²)²/4]dx = (2√2/3)√λ v³: finite, localised and permanent. A $(thing)pocket of false vacuum$() is the same idea in reverse: a region left in the higher valley, held by its own wall, waiting.

The $(item)Higgs Field Modulator$() quenches a $(item)Metastable Vacuum Lattice$() around a specimen in false vacuum and catches the seams as $(item)Topological Defect Cores$(). They are where the branch's physics leaks into everything else.
A knot in a broken symmetry: the field could not agree which vacuum to fall into, so it kept both - and the seam between them cannot untie.$(br2)Made in $(item)Higgs Field Modulator$().
The Higgs potential mapped out to the Planck scale: the valley we live in is not the deepest one. Held in a lattice of Higgs field capacitors.$(br2)Made in $(item)Higgs Field Modulator$().
